samples.summary: Frontend API-keys visibility change has no test at all
samples.evidence: workspace-settings.tsx now (a) renders the API Keys section unconditionally instead of `isOwner &&`, (b) enables the fetchApiKeys query for every member, and (c) adds an owner-only "Created by" column fed by `creatorName(apiKey.createdBy)`. The sole frontend test file for this page (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-settings.test.tsx) mocks `fetchApiKeys`/`createApiKey`/`revokeApiKey` (lines 26-28) but never sets a resolved value and never asserts anything about API keys — its three tests cover only member/invite controls. So nothing fails if the section regresses to owner-only, if the query stays disabled for members, or if the Created by column renders for non-owners / maps to the wrong username. This is the user-facing half of the feature and the file already demonstrates the exact owner/non-owner rendering pattern needed.
searchedFor: Grep 'api-key|apiKey|API Key' under packages/frontend/src (6 files, none a settings test)

samples.summary: No test that a member-minted key actually works against /api/v1, nor that it is confined to that member's authority
samples.evidence: The motivating claim of the change (controller doc comment, plus the rewritten comments in api/v1/documents.controller.ts:178 and folders.controller.ts:68 — "a plain member's key deletes only their own documents", "renames but does not move or delete somebody else's folder") describes a newly reachable path: before this change only owners could mint keys, so a member-authority key never hit the v1 manager checks. The new e2e test only exercises the /workspaces/:id/api-keys management endpoints; the only Bearer-token v1 exercise is the pre-existing owner-key lifecycle test (lines 92-153). Nothing asserts a member key can read v1 at all, and nothing asserts a member key is refused when deleting another user's document/folder — a wrong answer there destroys data.

samples.summary: E2E revocation asserts only the 200 status, not that the key was actually revoked
samples.evidence: The new scoping test does `DELETE .../api-keys/${memberKey.body.id}` expecting 200 and stops there. Since revoke was rewritten from `update` to `updateMany` + read-back, a where-clause that matched but wrote nothing (or a data payload regression) would still return 200 with a body. A follow-up assertion (list now empty, or the raw key rejected 401 as in the lifecycle test at line 149) would make the test actually prove revocation.

samples.summary: No test pins the read-back's workspace scoping in revoke
samples.evidence: revoke's `findUnique({ where: { id } })` (api-key.service.ts:108-109) drops workspaceId/createdBy, but every unit test only asserts on `updateMany`'s where or on the select object; the read-back's where clause is never asserted. (Whether that omission is itself a bug is the correctness lens's call — the test-side point is that no assertion would notice a change there.)

samples.summary: The 'without its hash' assertion is near-tautological
samples.evidence: `expect(prisma.apiKey.findUnique.mock.calls[0][0].select.hashedKey).toBeUndefined()` passes for any select literal that simply omits the field, and would also pass for `hashedKey: false`. It only catches the (throwing) case of no select at all. Asserting the whole select object, or that the returned value has no hashedKey key, would state the intent directly.

samples.summary: creatorName's "Unknown" fallback (creator no longer in members) is untested
samples.evidence: `creatorName` falls back to "Unknown" when the creator is not among workspace.members — a real case (member removed after minting a key, owner still sees the key). No frontend test exercises creatorName at all.

searchedFor: Grep 'api-key|apiKey|API Key' under packages/frontend/src (6 files, none a settings test)

verdict.reason: The component changes exist as described: the API Keys section renders unconditionally (workspace-settings.tsx:433-505, contrast the isOwner gates at :356 and :508), the fetchApiKeys query is enabled for every member (:146-150), and an owner-only "Created by" column is fed by creatorName(apiKey.createdBy) (:153-155, :460, :473-477). The only file in the repo that renders WorkspaceSettings is workspace-settings.test.tsx (grep for WorkspaceSettings across packages/ returns just the component, this test, App.tsx, and a design-sandbox scene config). That test mocks fetchApiKeys/createApiKey/revokeApiKey with no resolved value (:26-28) and asserts only on member/invite controls (:110-178) — nothing about API keys. Searched wide for a counterexample: grep for "API Keys|Created by|Revoke API key|Create API Key" across packages/ yields only the component, docs, a non-asserting design-sandbox fixture (design-sandbox/src/scenes/fixtures/workspace.ts:6), the CLI, and backend/test/api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts (server-side scoping, not frontend rendering); grep for createdBy|creatorName in the frontend yields no test. api/url.test.ts:106-108 exercises the API functions only for path-traversal URL encoding and never renders the page. No frontend e2e suite exists. So a user-facing behavior change has no test that could fail if the section regressed to owner-only, the query stayed disabled for members, or the Created by column leaked to non-owners — a major missing-test gap in this lens's lane.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim — that nothing asserts a member-authority API key is refused when deleting/moving another user's document or folder — is contradicted by existing unit specs the reviewer did not search (they only grepped packages/backend/test). documents.controller.spec.ts:91-97 ("forbids an API key whose minter is no longer a manager") drives the real ApiV1DocumentsController.remove with an API-key identity req(MEMBER, true, ['read','write']) against a document authored by AUTHOR, asserting ForbiddenException AND that deleteDocument was never called. folders.controller.spec.ts:294-299 does the same for folder delete, and folders.controller.spec.ts:263-268 covers the exact "does not move somebody else's folder" clause quoted from the doc comment, with the complementary positive (member may rename) at 169-176. These are not over-mocked: the controllers are constructed for real (documents.controller.spec.ts:45-52, folders.controller.spec.ts:76-79) and use the real isDocumentManager helper (documents.controller.ts:192, folders.controller.ts:86, document/document-access.ts:16); only the role lookup and persistence are stubbed, so the tests fail if the authority check is weakened. The residual half of the claim (no end-to-end assertion that a member key can read v1 at all) is partly covered by the role-agnostic accept path in workspace-scope.guard.ts:40-45 tested at workspace-scope.guard.spec.ts:31-41 and by api-key.controller.spec.ts:49; and its failure mode is a loud 403 on first use, not the data destruction on which the finding's major severity rests.
